skill.name: pytm
skill.description: Create and maintain pytm threat models with Python examples, STRIDE review steps, CI guidance, and diagram troubleshooting for security architecture work.
skill.summary: Use pytm to model architecture, identify STRIDE threats, and document mitigations as code.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md. Most static findings are Markdown formatting, inline code, or reference URLs. A few command examples install packages, run local Python files, or use sudo, so agents should require explicit approval and a trusted environment.

remediation.suggestion: Avoid sudo in skill instructions where possible. Mark Linux package installation as a user-approved or CI-only action.
State that agents should only run threat_model.py and helper scripts from trusted repositories after user confirmation.
Recommend virtual environments, pinned dependency versions, and official installation sources for pytm and Graphviz.

content.user_title: Build pytm Threat Models as Code
content.value_statement: Threat modeling often becomes outdated and disconnected from architecture changes. This skill helps create pytm models, STRIDE analysis, and diagram workflows for security reviews and CI.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of pytm threat models with actors, boundaries, components, and data flows.
Explains STRIDE review steps for spoofing, tampering, repudiation, disclosure, denial, and privilege risks.
Provides Python examples for web, microservice, custom threat, trust boundary, and scoring patterns.
Shows CI workflow concepts for generating diagrams, reports, and mitigation checks.
Covers security handling for sensitive architecture details, reports, repositories, and review records.
Lists troubleshooting steps for missing threats, Graphviz diagrams, false positives, and model drift.
limitations: The package only contains SKILL.md; referenced scripts and templates are not bundled.
It cannot validate a real architecture without accurate user-provided components, boundaries, and data flows.
Command examples may install packages or run local Python, so agents need user approval.
pytm threat output still requires human review for likelihood, impact, and mitigation quality.

use_cases.title: Design Review Preparation
use_cases.description: Create a first pytm model before an architecture review and document key STRIDE threats.

use_cases.title: CI Threat Model Checks
use_cases.description: Add model generation and mitigation checks to a pipeline for architecture changes.

use_cases.title: Application Security Documentation
use_cases.description: Convert service boundaries, sensitive data flows, and mitigations into reviewable threat model documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Web Threat Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a pytm threat model for a three-tier web application. Include actors, trust boundaries, data flows, and initial STRIDE concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Flows
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this architecture description for pytm modeling. Identify missing boundaries, sensitive flows, and security attributes before I write the model.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CI Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI workflow for a pytm model that generates diagrams, produces a threat report, and flags unmitigated high-risk threats.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Threat Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define organization-specific pytm threats, risk scoring criteria, and mitigation documentation for API and cloud storage controls.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a threat model for an e-commerce web application with a web server and database.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a structured model plan with actors, boundaries, encrypted flows, STRIDE concerns, and mitigation review steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants pytm checks during pull requests.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines dependency setup, diagram generation, artifact upload, and a mitigation gate for the CI workflow.

output_examples.input: A security lead needs to reduce irrelevant threats.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends accurate component properties, threat conditions, documented exclusions, and periodic review of model drift.

best_practices: Keep threat models near architecture documentation and review them when boundaries or data flows change.
Use placeholders for credentials, tokens, customer data, and internal network details.
Run generated commands only in trusted repositories, controlled virtual environments, or CI runners.
anti_patterns: Treating generated STRIDE threats as final risk decisions without human review.
Publishing diagrams or reports that reveal sensitive architecture details.
Running local threat model scripts from untrusted repositories without approval.

faq.question: Does this skill include executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. The audited package only includes SKILL.md, so referenced scripts and templates must be supplied separately.

faq.question: Can it generate data flow diagrams?
faq.answer: It explains how pytm and Graphviz generate diagrams, but the user must provide a valid model and installed dependencies.

faq.question: Is it suitable for CI pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides CI workflow guidance for model generation, artifacts, and mitigation checks.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It supports analysis, but security teams must validate threats, likelihood, impact, and mitigations.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Clear architecture descriptions with actors, trust boundaries, components, protocols, sensitive data, and existing controls work best.

faq.question: What should agents avoid?
faq.answer: Agents should avoid running install commands, sudo commands, or local Python files without explicit user approval.
